   filtering is at 16 everywhere, since it is cheap and looks better at steep angles. So every

   and table samplers that are not textures keep their own filters. The game's textures read through

   nothing. Added at 11:40, the game is pixel filtering and needs no change, so its atlas stays at

off again (`placeOf`), and the `world` of a pixel is its place plus the origin, so every use below
reads as before. With the game's origin on, the world numbers stay under about 5,000 blocks, where a
float's step is a 2,048th of a block, and none of them shows.

  again. `lightReachingPlaced(pixelMiddle(input.place, ...))` snaps to the same eighths, the

The game's side of the engine's part 7, read on 6.2.60 with the game at `f201940` as it ships, from
copies of the review's copy of the data, at 1280 by 720 with the frame unlimited, under the
exclusive lock on tuned's powersave-bazzite, three runs.

What `Recenter` does in its frame (`VoxelGame.cs:546-564`), called from `Begin` (`:645`) before
anything is stepped or drawn. The step is to the multiple of 1,024 nearest the player once it is
4,096 out along x or z (`LandOrigin.cs:84-98`), so a walk or a flight moves the origin 4,096 at once
and a teleport by any multiple of 1,024, and y never moves. In order:

1. `Renderer.Shift` (`ChunkRenderer.cs:952-984`) uploads every section part's mesh again, uploads
   the lamps' cubes again (`MakeLampCubes`, `:679`), gives every part and group a new `Transform`,
   moves the emitters' matrices, marks every group's faces changed and has the lamps gathered again.
2. Every ECS `Body`, the player's and the camera with it, every arrow and every blast moves by the
   step.
3. The mobs' homes and last places (`Mob.cs:193`), the fall's last height (`Vitals.cs:74`), the
   steps' voices (`GameSounds.cs:88`), the blasts' clouds and flashes, set again in the engine by
   `SetParticleEmitterPosition` and `SetLightPosition` (`BlastEffects.cs:112-124`), the bits' bodies
   (`BlockBits.cs:88`) and the rings on the water (`AmbientParticles.cs:137`) move by it.
4. `LandOrigin.MoveTo` last. The held torch's light is set from the hand the next frame, and the sky
   takes no place.

So the engine is handed again every section's mesh as a new one, every part's matrix moved by the
step, the lamps' cubes as new meshes and the camera moved by the step, all in one frame.

  and, at High, `cpu.global_illumination` 164 ms, the ray scene built again for every mesh.

anything moves, in the update of the frame whose draws the engine then extracts, the call with the

The mend is the play's alone, each wait bounded:

  seed's step presses a key.
- The seed's step reads the world's name before Escape and, after Enter, reads the state until it
  names another world, twenty times at most, where it read once three frames after.
- The run that keeps its files waits for its world to stand before F2, which only a frame of play
  takes, where it waited 30 frames.

The play's two other openings, the first and the overworld's, wait by `stood`.

The play's script alone changes, so no build or suite was run for it. The play, under the lock taken
exclusive with no quiet wait on the GPU, passes in 187 s, its seed's step naming the overworld of
seed 12345 in 5 s, its `captures/closed.log` naming nothing left at a close 0.53 s after the new
world, and its captures within 9 levels of the warm play's on 6.2.102, `sky2.png` differing in 0.10%
of its pixels past 8 levels, the most 116. A play on the GPU passed before the mend too, its respawn
standing in a few frames.

Verdict 15's read. The engine's walk for slangc changed between 6.2.86 and 6.2.102, in its commit
`b634f33d`, "the shader compiler is taken from the nearest checkout of the engine alone and only
where the user owns it". At 6.2.86 `SlangCompiler.Locate` walked up from the program's folder and
from the working directory and took `build/tools/slang/bin/slangc` in any folder it passed, so the
play's game in `VoxelSandbox/bin/Debug/net10.0` found the one `build/fetch-slang.sh` puts in the
game's checkout, and compiled the terrain shader there on a runner whose cache was empty. The green
run of `fc4a632` on 6.2.86 logs no "slangc was not found" where the red one logs it. At 6.2.102 the
walk (`SlangCompiler.FromCheckout`) stops at the nearest folder that holds `3DEngine.slnx` and takes
its `build/tools` alone, so a game's checkout, which holds `VoxelSandbox.slnx`, gives none, and a
game on the package finds slangc only by `ENGINE_SLANGC`. That is the engine's change, made on
purpose so no program runs a compiler from a folder others may write, and the game names its own:

- The build workflow's play job and the pack workflow's shaders job name `ENGINE_SLANGC` as the
  checkout's slangc once `build/fetch-slang.sh` has fetched it.
- `build/play.sh` and `build/shaders.sh` name the checkout's slangc where none is named, so a local
  run needs no setting.
- `build/fetch-slang.sh` and `build/fetch-slang.ps1` end by saying the line that names it, and their
  notes and the README's Running it say the engine looks in a checkout of the engine alone.

The pack workflow's `build/shaders.sh` runs `./e3d shaders` out of `.engine`, whose `build/tools`
holds no slangc, so it would have failed the same way on 6.2.102. A packed game carries the shaders
it compiled and needs no compiler, which a pack run after the build proves.

The scripts, the workflows and the README alone change, so no build or suite was run for them. A
play with an empty cache and no `ENGINE_SLANGC` set, `slangc` fetched into the game's checkout as
the workflow fetches it, under the lock taken exclusive with no quiet wait, passes in 287 s,
compiling terrain.slang in frame 225, its `captures/closed.log` naming nothing left at a close 0.57
s after the new world, and its captures within 8 levels of the warm play's on 6.2.102, `sky2.png`
differing in 0.02% of its pixels past 8 levels.

Item 222's mends, each with a test that passes three runs in three and fails on a copy of the head:

  `A_Game_Whose_Interface_Pack_Holds_Metadata_Of_Other_Kinds_Draws_Its_Sprites_Without_It` opens a

  which on the head ends at the first frame of the HUD, and
  `A_Blocks_Metadata_Of_Other_Kinds_Than_It_Takes_Is_Read_As_None_And_Said_Once` reads a block's

- A default pack in the folder whose file cannot be read threw as the packs' screen opened. It

  `A_Default_Pack_That_Cannot_Be_Read_Counts_As_Missing_And_Is_Said_Once`, a pack's file refused to

Item 223's mends, each with a test that passes three runs in three and fails on a copy of the head
given the seams it names:

- A request to end the process, the signal a session's close, a kill by name or Control and C sends,
  ends the frames as the window's close does (`Program.cs`), so the closing save runs.
  `A_Request_To_End_The_Process_Saves_The_World_As_The_Windows_Close_Does` runs the game as a
  program of its own with no window, on a data folder of the test's own, sends it the signal once
  its world stands, and finds it ended with code 0 and the world's info written. On the head it ends
  with code 143 and nothing saved.
- A run takes a lock file in its data folder for as long as it runs (`running.lock`, which the
  system lets go as the process ends however it ends), and a run that cannot take it, as a second
  run opened on the folder, keeps nothing there, saying so on the HUD.
  `A_Run_Opened_On_A_Data_Folder_Another_Run_Holds_Says_So_And_Writes_Nothing_There`, the lock held
  by the test, a block set, the world saved and the options kept, and neither the world's info nor
  the options file written. On the head both are.
- A column's blocks that inflate short of a column, or of the eight sections a column of a world
  that stood from 0 to 128 holds, or with a part of a section left over, are read as unreadable
  (`WorldSave.Decode`), so the column is generated again and its region's file copied aside.
  `A_Columns_Blocks_That_Inflate_Short_Of_A_Column_Are_Read_As_Unreadable`, ten sections, eight and
  a part, and one short of a whole column and a part, with a whole column and the eight of an old
  one read. On the head each is read as a column.
- A screenshot is said saved once its file stands whole, ending with the chunk a PNG ends with,
  since the engine writes it in its place after the frame, and said not written where it does not
  stand within five seconds (`VoxelGame.ShotSeconds`), the engine's log saying why.
  `A_Screenshot_Is_Said_Saved_Once_Its_File_Stands_Whole_And_Said_Not_Written_Where_It_Does_Not`
  writes the picture as the engine writes it, cut short and then whole, and lets a second go

Item 224's read, by three readers in parallel over the rules that change blocks, the light, mobs and
stacks, and the blocks that tick with the streamer's own order of joining and letting go. Much
stands guarded at the edge. A mob thinks and moves only with the columns about it loaded and is kept
once by the column its middle stands in, a falling block over a column that unloads is set down in
it first, no change reaches a column being made, fires resume once on a column's return, furnaces
wait while their column is away, and the timed save holds the streamer still while it writes. The
high findings are mended in three commits, each with a test at a column's border that passes three
runs in three and fails on a copy of the head given the seams it names:

- `f3c7c20`, the game.
  - A chest's window left open as a jump let its column go began an empty chest there each frame,
    which on the column's return kept the saved chest's items out and was saved in their place. The
    window of a chest or a furnace whose column is not loaded shuts,
    `A_Chests_Window_Open_As_The_Player_Leaves_For_Far_Land_Keeps_The_Chest_It_Shows`.
  - A felling under way as the world was switched or closed, or the player jumped, left its tree's
    upper logs and crown standing over the cut, saved so, and its steps ran on in the next world at
    the same places, breaking its leaves and logs and wearing the axe of its hotbar. The steps still
    to go are taken at once as the world is left, closed or jumped from, and a world opened lets go
    of any felling,
    `A_Felling_Under_Way_As_The_World_Is_Left_Is_Taken_Whole_Before_Its_Save_And_Goes_No_Further`.
  - Sand or gravel loosened after the frame's own fall and before an unload, a jump or a close was
    kept as air, and fell next frame into the column let go, landing at once as an item there. What
    was loosened, felled or let fall is taken before the streamer, a jump or a close lets go of
    anything, so it is set down as a block,
    `Sand_Loosened_As_The_World_Is_Left_Or_A_Jump_Leaves_Its_Column_Is_Set_Down_As_A_Block`, the
    switch and the jump each failing on the head alone.
  - A felling read a column not loaded as holding no log, so leaves held by a log across the border
    decayed. Leaves within reach of a column not loaded are spared and asked again each frame once
    every column about them is loaded, those then loose of every log decaying,
    `A_Fellings_Leaves_Beside_A_Column_Not_Loaded_Stand_Until_It_Joins_And_Are_Asked_Again_Then`.
- `c69fcb5`, the streamer and the save.
  - A world that keeps no save, a transient run, a run on a data folder another holds or one whose
    folder could not be made, made a changed column again from its generator as it came back, the
    chests and furnaces kept in memory then spilling. Its changed columns are held for the run in
    the order they were let go,
    `A_Column_Changed_In_A_World_That_Keeps_No_Save_Holds_Its_Change_Through_A_Jump_Away_And_Back`.
    A changed column of the overworld holds 2.4 to 4.3 KB, 3.1 KB on the mean of 24 read, and one of
    the flat world 227 bytes, so a long transient run grows by about 3 KB for each column it changes
    and leaves. They are held to 256 MB, some 85,000 such columns, past which those let go longest
    ago are given up and the log says so once, which the test reads with the bound set to a byte.
  - A jump left the columns made or being made for the place left to join there afterward, their
    mobs and stacks put back at float places about an origin moved far off. Those columns are let go
    at the jump and a worker's column made for a place left is dropped,
    `Columns_Made_For_A_Place_The_Player_Left_Do_Not_Join_There`.
  - A region whose file was held for a passing fault let go of what its columns kept, blocks, mobs
    and chests, at the first save of the run, so walking away and back lost them for the run. A held
    region stays in memory for the run,
    `A_Region_Held_For_A_Passing_Fault_Keeps_What_Its_Columns_Hold_For_The_Run`.
- The commit carrying this Reply, the water. Waiting flow on a column that unloaded was let go, and
  its return asked only the water facing air across its edges, so a flood or a stream drying in it
  stood frozen, saved so, and water fed from across the edge of a column not loaded dried back where
  something asked it. Every flowing cell of a column that arrives is asked again, with the flowing
  water across its edges, a source left alone, and water beside a column not loaded keeps its level,
  `A_Flood_Half_Spread_As_Its_Column_Unloads_Goes_On_As_The_Column_Arrives_Again` and
  `Water_Fed_Across_The_Edge_Of_A_Column_Not_Loaded_Keeps_Its_Level_Until_It_Arrives`. The README
  and the water's remarks say so.

Read and left, the lows:

- Light from a source across a column that was away when the source went stays until a block beside
  it changes or the land loads again, light being worked out afresh at each load.
- `voxel.restock` places a column's herd again where the herd walked into the next column, a command
  the player runs on purpose.
- Lit TNT over a column an ordinary walk lets go burns out there and breaks nothing, and a close
  within its fuse leaves no block.
- An explosion's rays pass a column not loaded as air and break nothing in it, and fire neither
  spreads into nor is fed from one.
- An arrow stuck at a pending column hangs once the column arrives, for its minute.
- A column pending or left out reads as solid to the player and to stacks, an unseen wall until it
  arrives.
- A timed save keeps neither falling blocks nor lit TNT until they land, and a fire's age begins
  again on its column's return.
- Water levels across an edge go stale while a column is away until a block beside them changes.
- A held chests file gives a generated chest its loot again for the run.
- The mobs of a column's neighbors stand frozen beside a column left out.
- Leaves spared beside a column not loaded stand for good where the world closes before the column
  arrives.
- Logs across the border of a column not loaded are not felled with their tree and stand once it
  arrives.
- Stacks of items are not saved, item 225.

skipped, 592, 595 and 597 passing, the headless game's 83, 85 and 85 passing three times in a row,
